R3A-bear-backcountry-0004.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R3A-bear-backcountry-0004.parkWhat: pull off on Hwy 99 (Soo River Bridge) (paved road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2011 (15 years old), 80 m SE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
S facing slope, 18 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Rutherford Creek 170 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

flags.t: Route touches city limits: Village of Pemberton. Local firearm bylaw applies.

plan: Drive: from Resort Municipality of Whistler, about 24 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Hwy 99.
Park: 50.25842, -122.86382, pull off on Hwy 99 (Soo River Bridge) (paved road). Map links below.
Walk: 9.3 km W, on Hwy 99. Climb about 735 m, about 260 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 360 m SE of the spot at 731 m (50.28445, -122.96955). Water: Rutherford Creek right here (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 2-11, Region 2. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
